question_text: Two plane mirrors are placed perpendicular to each other as shown in the figure. An object $O$ is kept at the angular bisector of the two mirrors. The number of images of object $O$ formed will be
diagram_description: Two perpendicular plane mirrors oriented along the coordinate axes with an object O positioned on the angle bisector between them.
solution: Here, $\theta = 90^\circ$. Since $\frac{360^\circ}{\theta} = \frac{360^\circ}{90^\circ} = 4$ is an even integer, the number of images is $n = \frac{360^\circ}{\theta} - 1 = 4 - 1 = 3$.

question_text: A plane mirror is placed at the bottom of a fish tank filled with water of refractive index $\frac{4}{3}$. The fish is at a height $10\text{ cm}$ above the plane mirror. An observer $O$, vertically above the fish outside the water, sees the fish and its image in the mirror. The apparent distance between the fish and its image is
diagram_description: A fish tank containing water with a horizontal plane mirror at the bottom. A fish is at a height of 10 cm above the mirror, and an observer is situated vertically above the fish outside the tank.
solution: The actual distance between the fish and its image in the mirror is $d = 10\text{ cm} + 10\text{ cm} = 20\text{ cm}$. When viewed from air, the apparent distance is $d' = \frac{d}{\mu} = \frac{20}{4/3} = 15\text{ cm}$.

question_text: A beam of light consisting of red, green and blue colours is incident normally on a right-angled prism as shown. The refractive indices of the material of the prism for red, green and blue wavelengths are $1.39$, $1.44$ and $1.47$ respectively. Which of the three colours will come out of the right face of the prism?
diagram_description: A right-angled isosceles prism with base angle 45 degrees. A horizontal ray containing red, green, and blue light enters normally through the vertical face and strikes the hypotenuse (right face) at an angle of incidence of 45 degrees.
solution: The angle of incidence at the hypotenuse face is $i = 45^\circ$. Total internal reflection occurs if $\mu > \frac{1}{\sin 45^\circ} = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$. Since $\mu_{\text{red}} = 1.39 < 1.414$, red will refract out, while green and blue undergo TIR.

question_text: A light ray is incident on a prism of refracting angle $30^\circ$. One face of the prism is silvered as shown in the figure. If the refractive index of the prism is $\sqrt{2}$, then for what value of angle of incidence will the ray retrace its path?
diagram_description: A triangular prism with apex angle 30 degrees having its second face silvered. A ray incidents at angle i on the first face and strikes the silvered face normally.
solution: For the ray to retrace its path, it must hit the silvered face normally, so $r_2 = 0^\circ$. Thus, $r_1 = A - r_2 = 30^\circ$. Using Snell's law: $\sin i = \mu \sin r_1 = \sqrt{2} \sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \implies i = 45^\circ$.

question_text: A plane mirror is fixed in the $yz$-plane at $x = 0$. The velocity of a moving object is $\vec{v}_o = -3\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$. The velocity of the image relative to a stationary observer will be
diagram_description: A coordinate system showing the y-axis, with the plane mirror located along x = 0 (yz-plane), and an object vector v_o moving in the second quadrant toward the y-axis.
solution: For a mirror lying in the $yz$-plane, reflection reverses only the component of velocity perpendicular to the mirror (the $x$-component): $v_{ix} = -v_{ox} = 3\hat{i}$, while parallel components remain unchanged ($6\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$).

question_text: If the space between two convex lenses of glass in the combination shown in the figure below is filled with water, then the
options: Focal length of the system will decrease
Focal length of the system will increase
Power of system will become infinite
diagram_description: Two convex lenses placed facing each other with an enclosed space in between them that forms a biconcave water lens when filled.
solution: The water layer forms a diverging (concave) lens of negative power ($P_w < 0$). The net power of the system decreases ($P_{\text{net}} = P_1 + P_2 + P_w$), which causes the equivalent focal length ($F = 1/P_{\text{net}}$) to increase.
